channel.title: MYRSS Daily Digest
channel.description: Ten curated selections, two each from de Volkskrant, New York Times, Follow the Money, Reuters and The New Yorker. Priority: last 48 hours. Source RSS feeds were last refreshed around 07:00 UTC on 22 November 2026; later developments may be absent. Most descriptions are RSS-based; Reuters selections checked against original reporting.

item.title: de Volkskrant | Akkoord over moordrobots verder uit zicht, VS en Rusland willen niet
item.description: De Volkskrant reports that efforts to reach a binding agreement on lethal autonomous weapons remain stalled, with the United States and Russia opposing restrictions. Based on the publisher's RSS headline.

item.title: de Volkskrant | Russische media: Topvrouw grootste Russische webshop Wildberries treedt af na plaatsing op sanctielijst EU
item.description: According to Russian media cited by de Volkskrant, the head of Wildberries has stepped down after inclusion on an EU sanctions list. Based on RSS headline reporting.

item.title: New York Times | Deadly Protests Erupt in Bangladesh Over Exiled Former Leader. What to Know.
item.description: The New York Times reports deadly unrest involving supporters of exiled former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who was sentenced to death in absentia. Based on RSS summary.

item.title: New York Times | China’s Spies Set Sights on A.I. Chips Years Before Nvidia Scandal
item.description: The New York Times reports allegations by officials that China's intelligence agency pursued advanced AI chips and related intelligence years before the recent Nvidia scandal. Based on RSS summary.

item.title: Follow the Money | Hoe cocaïnegeld België binnendringt: ‘Het zat vroeger niet zo diep in het systeem’
item.description: FTM interviews senior Belgian justice officials about the penetration of cocaine proceeds into Belgium and the difficulty of disrupting trafficking's business model. Based on RSS summary.

item.title: Follow the Money | FTM25: Deutsche Bank, China en de Woo
item.description: FTM's 25-minute podcast revisits its reporting on Deutsche Bank, China and Dutch freedom-of-information requests. A recap rather than a new investigation; based on RSS summary.

item.title: Reuters | Myanmar's army-backed government calls ASEAN decision 'unfair and imbalanced'
item.description: Myanmar's military-backed authorities criticised ASEAN's decision to deny them full representation at summits, calling it discriminatory. Checked against Reuters' original report.

item.title: Reuters | Denmark pushes EU to tighten travel curbs on Russians after foiled plot
item.description: Denmark urged EU-wide restrictions on Russian tourist visas and non-biometric passports after Danish authorities alleged a Russian-backed assassination plot. Russia disputes the accusation. Checked against Reuters' original report.

item.title: The New Yorker | Matt Salinger Doesn’t Know Where the Ducks Go
item.description: Matt Salinger reflects on his father J. D. Salinger's novel The Catcher in the Rye and Holden Caulfield's famous question about the ducks in Central Park. Based on RSS summary.

item.title: The New Yorker | Reading in Reverse
item.description: A personal essay experiments with reading a book backwards, sentence by sentence. Based on RSS summary.
